source.title: Intrinsic Dimension, Persistent Homology and Generalization in Neural Networks
source.authors: Tolga Birdal; Aaron Lou; L. Guibas; Umut Simsekli

record.tranche_reason: The study measures persistent-homology dimension of training trajectories and compares it with train–test performance gaps, using a different measure from the magnitude-aware sharpness named in V7. It also tests a topological regularizer's effect on test accuracy.
record.gate_note: The paper reports persistent-homology dimension versus test accuracy or generalization gap, plus a topological-regularization experiment. It does not test the specific interventions or outcomes in V1–V6 or V8, or the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7. Values visible only in plots are recorded as figure only; no plotted values are estimated.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether persistent-homology dimension predicts generalization and whether a topological regularizer improves accuracy. Neither is a claim version here. Trajectory dimension does not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. Using several architectures, optimizers and batch sizes does not itself establish the performance comparisons specified in V3–V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report that trajectory persistent-homology dimension correlates with generalization across tested networks and optimizers, and present topological regularization as a proof of concept for improving accuracy, especially under poorer training settings. The accuracy difference at learning rate 0.01 is not statistically significant.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates a topological dimension of training trajectories and proposes a topological training regularizer; it does not reproduce the claim versions' specified interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports varying relationships across batch sizes; for LeNet-5, the regularizer's test-accuracy difference was not statistically significant at learning rate 0.01, unlike the other tested rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower estimated persistent-homology dimension accompanies smaller generalization gaps or higher test accuracy. AlexNet+SGD on CIFAR100 has Kendall coefficients 0.933, 0.357 and 0.733 at batch sizes 64, 100 and 128.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Persistent-homology dimension of training trajectories can predict generalization within the tested settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Topological regularization improves LeNet-5 CIFAR10 test accuracy significantly at four tested learning rates; the difference at 0.01 is nonsignificant. Estimated trajectory dimension decreases at all five rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Penalizing trajectory persistent-homology dimension can improve test accuracy in some LeNet-5 CIFAR10 training regimes.

record.problems: The generalization associations are primarily presented in plots without per-condition numerical values; the stated Kendall correlations cover AlexNet with SGD on CIFAR100 at three batch sizes. The paper reports a simple-architecture proof of concept for regularization and does not provide numerical test accuracies in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Synthetic diffusion intrinsic-dimension estimator comparisons and figure visualizations were left out because they do not measure network generalization outcomes.

untested.parts: Paired random-label memorization and natural-label generalization experiments.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional-versus-fully-connected performance comparisons, local-connectivity interventions and transferred initialization.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance comparisons under defined tuning budgets and recovery recipes.
Large-versus-small batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence and removal alongside weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to the specified claim versions; they do not deny the reported dimension correlations or regularization effects. No version-specific verdict follows from replacing sharpness with a different complexity measure.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and generalization on natural labels.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold.
Controlled convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity interventions.
Adaptive-optimizer versus SGD held-out performance comparisons under specified tuning regimes.
Large-batch versus small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions and their effects across training-set sizes or augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: AlexNet
rows.operation_detail: Compare estimated persistent-homology dimension of training trajectories with training–test accuracy gap.

conditions.value: varying; individual values not stated in the result text

rows.measure: Association between estimated persistent-homology dimension and generalization error (training accuracy - test accuracy).
rows.value: Figure only; text says the dimension is directly correlated with the generalization error and that the pattern is consistent across datasets and optimizers.
rows.note: The figure plots points and best-fit lines; numerical values for each setting are not stated in the text.
rows.check: The reported association concerns trajectory dimension, not any specified version. Figure 3 explicitly gives batch sizes 64, 100 and 128; the condition should include them.

rows.subject: AlexNet

rows.measure: Kendall correlation coefficient between dimension and test gap.
rows.locator: Section 5.1, “Is dimPH a real indicator of generalization?”
rows.note: The authors state that positive correlation signals the test gap closes as dimension decreases.
rows.check: The coefficient 0.933 is correctly extracted, but measures trajectory-dimension correlation rather than magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.measure: Relationship between persistent-homology dimension and test accuracy/generalization error.
rows.value: Figure only; text states that lower dimension accompanies higher test accuracy and that the measure correlates highly with generalization error.
rows.note: The result text describes a strong correlation; individual plotted values are not stated. The figure's model and dataset conditions are presented in aggregate.
rows.check: This aggregates dimension–performance associations, not a controlled architectural comparison. Figure 2 shows cnn-9 on MNIST and CIFAR10 and fcn-5/fcn-7 on MNIST, at batch sizes 50 and 100; Figure 3 separately concerns AlexNet on CIFAR10/CIFAR100. Avoid implying every architecture was evaluated on every dataset.

rows.subject: LeNet-5
rows.operation_detail: Train with the proposed topological regularizer, with λ set to 1, and compare test accuracy against clean training.
rows.baseline: Clean training; plotted values are figure only.
rows.value: Topological regularization; plotted values are figure only. Text says results differ with p < 0.05 for all cases except lr = 0.01, and describes higher accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: p < 0.05 for all cases except lr = 0.01
rows.note: The text says the improvement is most pronounced when learning rate/batch size normally results in poorer test accuracy; precise accuracies are only plotted.
rows.check: This compares the study's proposed topological regularizer with unregularized training, not dropout or another specified intervention. Split by learning rate if retaining these method-performance results: the accuracy difference is significant at the four lower rates and nonsignificant at 0.01.
